payload.description:
## Context
On a second machine, herdr restores Claude Code sessions after a restart but not Codex sessions. herdr restores only an agent that reported its session id through the herdr SessionStart hook.

On the first machine (WSL, herdr 0.9.5, codex-cli 0.166.0) every link exists: herdr integration status shows codex current v10, the user hooks.json calls the herdr hook script, config.toml sets features.hooks = true, and hooks.state holds a trusted_hash for the user session_start hook. A restart was not tested there.

terminal_setup installs the herdr integration (agents.py ensure_herdr_integrations) but never sets features.hooks and never reports whether Codex trusts the hook. A search of terminal_setup for features, trusted_hash and hooks found no such code.

Cause on the second machine: unknown. Candidates: an old or missing integration, a missing features.hooks flag, or an untrusted user hook. Assumed, not read from Codex documentation: Codex skips a hook that is disabled or untrusted.

Next: the owner runs these checks on the second machine.
herdr --version; herdr integration status | command grep -E 'claude|codex'
command grep -A2 '^\[features\]' ~/.codex/config.toml
command grep -c 'codex/hooks.json:session_start' ~/.codex/config.toml
payload.title: herdr does not restore codex sessions on a second machine

payload.text: 2026-11-05 checks on the second machine: herdr 0.9.5, codex integration current v10, features.hooks = true, 4 matches for codex/hooks.json:session_start. All three first candidates look fine. The count check was weak, because project hooks.json entries also match the pattern. The herdr codex hook script exits silently in these cases: HERDR_ENV, HERDR_SOCKET_PATH or HERDR_PANE_ID unset; python3 not on PATH; no transcript_path in the hook input; CODEX_THREAD_ID inherited from a parent Codex session and different from the new session id. The Claude hook has no CODEX_THREAD_ID check. Next check: herdr agent list while a codex pane runs, to see whether the codex entry has an agent_session.

2026-11-05 second machine, herdr agent list: 5 of 5 claude panes have an agent_session. 1 of 4 codex panes has one (w1:pF); w1:pJ, w1:pD and w1:pG have agent_session null. The user hook is trusted (2 exact matches for the user hooks.json session_start key). So the hook works for some Codex sessions and not others. Candidates: sessions started before the hook was installed or trusted; a fresh session whose SessionStart input has no transcript_path; CODEX_THREAD_ID inherited in the pane. Next: start a fresh codex in a new pane and compare with codex resume --last.

2026-11-05 likely cause, measured on the first machine: Codex 0.166.0 TUI sessions share one codex app-server daemon. The daemon processes carry HERDR_PANE_ID of the pane that started the daemon (measured from /proc environ: daemon w2:pB, the pane that started it). Assumed, not yet proven: SessionStart hooks run in the daemon, so every Codex session reports to the first pane, or to no pane, and other Codex panes keep agent_session null. This matches 1 of 4 codex panes with a session on the second machine. The user hook was trusted and active. A fresh codex had agent_session null before its first prompt. Not tested: a second Codex pane after a prompt. The fix belongs upstream in the herdr codex integration or Codex, not in terminal setup. Workaround to test: codex app-server daemon stop, then start Codex panes fresh.

2026-11-05 cause proven on the first machine (herdr 0.9.5, codex-cli 0.166.0). With no Codex daemon running, codex started in pane C, then in pane D. One shared codex app-server daemon served both, and its processes carried HERDR_PANE_ID of pane C (/proc environ). One prompt in pane D created session 01a1aab8-b8af-7341-a601-3f03bd8375bc. herdr agent list then showed that session on pane C and agent_session null on pane D. So the herdr codex SessionStart hook runs in the daemon and reports every Codex session to the pane that started the daemon. Other Codex panes have no session, and herdr cannot resume Codex there after a restart. The report happens at the first prompt, not at startup. Cleanup: both test panes closed, daemon stopped. Fix belongs upstream: the herdr codex integration needs a per-client pane identity, which a shared daemon environment cannot give. Terminal setup cannot fix it.

Integrated with origin/main c33bdd6 without discarding local history. Kept the newer remote responsiveness checks, both remote configuration tests and the reply contrast regression. Integrated verification: 721 tests passed; all 6 repository checks passed. Ledger fsck reported zero broken records and 11 warnings about identical copies of pre-existing events.

2026-11-05 upstream: already reported as herdrdev/herdr#4814 (open, triaged, p2), with confirmations on herdr 0.9.5 and WSL2. No new issue filed. Workaround from herdrdev/herdr#4649: codex features disable daemon_auto_start, then codex --no-daemon while a daemon still runs. Local codex 0.166.0 lists daemon_auto_start (stable, true) and --no-daemon. Saved wrong pane sessions stay wrong until the pane starts a new Codex session.
